traditions.d: Water-based colour woodblock printing, best known for ukiyo-e.
traditions.tech: Design glued to a block, cut away around the lines, inked with brush and printed with a baren; kentō marks register multiple blocks.

traditions.auth: Technique alone does not date a print, as workshops such as Adachi reproduce with the same methods; early impressions are the most valued.

traditions.d: Intaglio method of biting lines into a metal plate with acid, from Dürer and Hopfer to Rembrandt.
traditions.tech: Waxy ground scratched through with a needle, plate bitten in acid, inked, wiped and printed under pressure on damp paper.
traditions.mat: Copper, zinc or steel plate, hard or soft ground, ferric chloride or nitric acid
traditions.auth: Early impressions from a numbered edition are valued higher because plates wear; a plate may exist in several states.
